target.title: feat: unify Claude Code / Codex session catalogs into native session UX
target.body:
Closes #104598

## What Problem This Solves

The Claude session fleet (#104528) and Codex session catalog (#102586, #104045) surfaced external agent sessions in a bolted-on plugin tab: a custom hero/card layout, a bespoke read-only transcript viewer, a parallel sidebar section, and per-plugin RPC surfaces (`codex.sessions.*`, `anthropic.sessions.*`) that the Control UI special-cased by plugin id. External sessions looked and behaved nothing like native OpenClaw sessions, Claude rows could not be continued at all, and the Codex catalog was invisible unless `supervision.enabled` was set.

## Why This Change Was Made

External coding-agent sessions should feel like native sessions: rows in the normal sidebar, opened in the normal chat pane, and continuable by just typing. Core stays plugin-agnostic via a generic seam instead of hardcoded plugin ids.

- **Generic protocol + SDK seam.** New core gateway methods `sessions.catalog.list/read/continue/archive` (typebox schemas in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/sessions-catalog.ts`) dispatch to providers registered through the new typed SDK subpath `openclaw/plugin-sdk/session-catalog` (`api.registerSessionCatalog`). Catalog fan-out is deterministic and per-catalog error isolated. The unshipped per-plugin gateway methods are deleted with no aliases (no release tag contains them); the versioned node host commands are byte-stable for paired Mac nodes.
- **Native UI, custom views deleted.** Catalog sessions render as collapsible groups of native rows in the app sidebar and open in the regular chat pane in a read-only catalog mode (cursor-paginated "Load older", no live subscriptions). The custom views, controllers, sidebar element, styles, and plugin-tab wiring are deleted (~2.9k LOC removed; net diff is strongly negative).
- **Adopt-on-send.** Typing into a catalog session calls `sessions.catalog.continue`, navigates to the returned native session, and auto-sends the draft. Codex continues to use its supervision fork flow. Claude gains a new adoption path: the anthropic plugin creates a locked native session bound to the discovered Claude CLI session UUID, imports bounded visible history, and the first turn resumes with `--fork-session` so the source session is never mutated. A new generic one-shot fork lifecycle in the CLI runner (backend `forkArg`, binding `forkNextResume`, atomic claim/restore/successor persistence) backs this; forked resumes force a fresh CLI spawn so a cached warm stdio child can never run the turn inside the source session.
- **Plugin-owned session creation is fenced.** Plugins create adopted sessions only through a registry seam that verifies CLI-backend ownership, injects `pluginOwnerId`, and enforces the reserved `plugin:<pluginId>:` key namespace; the trusted create path applies seeded CLI bindings only for authorized plugin creations.
- **Zero-config visibility.** Codex catalog registration no longer requires `supervision.enabled`; that flag now gates only the agent-facing supervision tools. The anthropic catalog registers whenever the plugin loads (manifest `activation.onStartup: true`), needing no provider auth for local discovery.

## User Impact

Claude Code and Codex sessions across the Gateway and paired Macs appear in the normal sessions sidebar, open in the normal chat pane, and (for local idle CLI/VS Code sessions) can be continued by typing a message — the draft carries into the adopted native session and sends. Paired-node and Claude Desktop rows are view-only with an explanatory composer hint. No plugin tab, no custom UI. Codex users no longer need `supervision.enabled` just to see their sessions.

Out of scope (follow-ups): interacting with paired-node sessions (needs a node-side runner/streaming bridge per `docs/specs/codex-supervision.md`), sidebar pagination beyond the first 40 sessions per host (protocol cursors already support it), and live takeover of sessions owned by another running client.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox (delegated CI environment): `pnpm check:changed` + `pnpm test:changed` + `pnpm build` — green run on lease `tbx_01kx9jg9fdyefj10rx253a7v18` (Actions run 29169453351), on the branch rebased onto current `main`. Earlier failing runs (`tbx_01kx9e4sr7z6c9fbgpw3eafzd0`, `tbx_01kx9ev6qe5rs91kshnmjgjqza`, `tbx_01kx9f7kb6rd704xzmjq3qbzk7`, `tbx_01kx9hd1cnpg8h5h65xaktbqtb`) caught strict typecheck/lint/i18n/budget issues that are fixed in-branch; one `router-outlet.test.ts` failure was the known flake fixed by #104649 (confirmed unrelated: passes 3× in isolation on `tbx_01kx9h3k3dy74rchz47rk7dc6v`, and the branch now includes that deterministic fix via rebase). New UI strings are fully translated (i18n check reports zero recorded English fallbacks); the plugin SDK export budget bump (10540 → 10559) reflects the intentional new `session-catalog` subpath surface.
- UI e2e (Playwright against a mock gateway): `ui/src/e2e/claude-sessions.e2e.test.ts` (sidebar rows, transcript paging, view-only composer) and `ui/src/e2e/codex-sessions.e2e.test.ts` (adopt-on-send: continue RPC, navigation, draft auto-send).
- New unit coverage: gateway dispatch/fan-out isolation (`src/gateway/server-methods/session-catalog.test.ts`), registry ownership + namespace enforcement (`src/plugins/registry.runtime-config.test.ts`, `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-agent.test.ts`), one-shot fork lifecycle incl. claim/restore/successor and auth affinity (`src/agents/command/session-store.test.ts`, `src/agents/cli-runner/helpers.system-prompt-resume.test.ts`, `src/agents/cli-output.test.ts`), provider mapping (`extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.test.ts`, `extensions/codex/src/session-catalog.test.ts`), catalog key codec (`ui/src/lib/sessions/catalog-key.test.ts`).

target.title: fix(duckduckgo): forward abort signal when web search runs are canceled
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two cancellations bugs in the DuckDuckGo web search path:

1. **Dropped abort signal** — DuckDuckGo is the only web search provider that discards the caller's `AbortSignal`. While every other provider forwards `context?.signal` to its HTTP client, DDG drops it at the provider boundary. A canceled run leaves the DDG request open until its 20-second timeout expires.

2. **Fallback after cancellation** — Even after forwarding the signal, an aborted DDG request is caught by the shared `runWebSearch` catch block, which can start the next auto-detected provider. Canceling one provider should not trigger unintended fallback work.

## Why This Change Was Made

**DDG signal forwarding** (provider + client): Forward `context?.signal` through the DDG provider and client to `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint`, matching the pattern every other web search provider already uses (tavily #104965, searxng #104216, brave, exa, firecrawl, etc.). The entire chain already supports `signal?: AbortSignal` — DDG was simply the last provider not using it.

**Shared runtime abort guard** (`src/web-search/runtime.ts`): Add `params.signal?.throwIfAborted()` at the top of the provider loop and `params.signal?.aborted` in the catch block so a parent cancellation stops fallback immediately. This is the canonical pattern from #104216 — without it, forwarding the signal into a provider that then rejects on abort would still trigger the next auto-detected provider.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — abort through the guarded-fetch stack

A real stalled HTTP server (never sends headers) exercises the exact code path DDG uses: `withSelfHostedWebSearchEndpoint` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `fetch()`. Both `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint` (DDG's actual call) and `withSelfHostedWebSearchEndpoint` (used in this proof to allow localhost) share identical `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal({ signal })` → `fetch()` code paths; the only difference is the SSRF policy object.

```
[proof] Signal propagated in 123ms through guarded-fetch stack
        (withSelfHostedWebSearchEndpoint → fetchWithSsrFGuard → buildTimeoutAbortSignal → fetch)
[proof] stalled server: http://127.0.0.1:33563/stall
[proof] abort: controller.abort("proof: cancellation") @ ~100ms
[proof] error: DOMException: This operation was aborted
```

A held-open TCP connection is cancelled promptly (123ms) when the signal fires, rather than waiting for the configured 20-second timeout.

Proof script: `extensions/duckduckgo/proof/abort-guarded-fetch-proof.test.ts`

### Signal chain — full path (source verified)

| Layer | File | Line | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Web search runtime | `src/web-search/runtime.ts` | 475 | `params.signal?.throwIfAborted()` — terminal guard (new) |
| Web search runtime | `src/web-search/runtime.ts` | 489 | `definition.execute(params.args, { signal: params.signal })` |
| Web search runtime | `src/web-search/runtime.ts` | 503 | `params.signal?.aborted \|\| !allowFallback` — catch guard (new) |
| DDG provider tool | `extensions/duckduckgo/src/ddg-search-provider.ts` | 53 | `signal: context?.signal` (new) |
| DDG client | `extensions/duckduckgo/src/ddg-client.ts` | 201 | `signal: params.signal` (new) |
| Trusted endpoint wrapper | `src/agents/tools/web-search-provider-common.ts` | 105 | `signal: params.signal` → `withTrustedWebToolsEndpoint` |
| Guarded fetch router | `src/agents/tools/web-guarded-fetch.ts` | 88 | Spread `...params` → `withWebToolsNetworkGuard` |
| SSRF guard | `src/infra/net/fetch-guard.ts` | 496-498 | `buildTimeoutAbortSignal({ signal: params.signal })` |

No new SDK surface is needed — the entire chain already accepts `AbortSignal`.

### Test suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/duckduckgo/ src/web-search/runtime.test.ts
 ✓ DDG: 12/12 passed (including signal forwarding test)
 ✓ runtime: 31/31 passed (including "does not fall back after parent cancellation")
```

### Lint

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs \
    extensions/duckduckgo/src/ddg-search-provider.ts \
    extensions/duckduckgo/src/ddg-client.ts \
    extensions/duckduckgo/src/ddg-search-provider.test.ts \
    src/web-search/runtime.ts \
    src/web-search/runtime.test.ts
✓ clean
```

### Landing order

The `src/web-search/runtime.ts` abort guard is included here so this PR typechecks and tests standalone. #104216 (SearXNG, same author) also adds the same guard. Whichever PR lands first, the other will rebase; no cross-repo dependency.

target.title: fix(codex): do not promote missing_tool_result on abort/interrupt
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex app-server turns that end mid-exec (user abort, steer/interrupt, or other interrupt terminals) while a native `commandExecution` is still open would fail the whole attempt with a synthesized `missing_tool_result` prompt error. Operators then saw a generic tool-invariant failure instead of abort/interrupt classification, and any partial assistant text could be treated as a failed run.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the fail-closed synthetic `tool.result` rows for transcript/trajectory integrity, but stop promoting that invariant to the attempt `promptError` when the authoritative outcome is already `aborted` or turn status `interrupted`. Ordinary completed turns that still lack a matching tool result continue to record `promptError` as before. Failed-turn real errors remain preferred via the existing `this.promptError` assignment on `turn.status === "failed"`.

## User Impact

When a Codex-backed turn is cancelled or interrupted while a long-running native tool is still open, the attempt keeps abort/interrupt semantics instead of dying as a generic missing-tool invariant error. Partial assistant text on interrupted turns is preserved as non-error assistant output. Transcripts still show a synthetic failed tool result for the unfinished call.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS

### Current-main refresh

Merged latest `origin/main` into this branch (no force-push) so the projector guard and tests sit on current main after recent projector-adjacent refactors.

### Focused unit / projector regression (post-merge)

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts -t "does not promote missing_tool_result|records promptError when a completed turn has only whitespace"
# → 3 passed (abort mid-exec, interrupted pending tool, completed orphan control)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts
# → 148 passed
```

Focused proof excerpt:

```text
✓ does not promote missing_tool_result to promptError when aborted mid-exec
✓ does not promote missing_tool_result to promptError for interrupted turns with pending tools
✓ records promptError when a completed turn has only whitespace assistant text and an orphan tool call
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Live Codex app-server mid-exec interrupt must not promote synthetic `missing_tool_result` to run-level `promptError`, while still retaining the synthetic missing-tool detail for transcript integrity.
- Environment: local macOS; user `CODEX_HOME` (~/.codex) with existing Codex subscription auth; OpenClaw `createIsolatedCodexAppServerClient` (`homeScope=user`) + `CodexAppServerEventProjector` from this branch after main merge.
- Current-main contrast: Without the guard, `buildResult` would set `promptError` from the synthesized missing-tool string whenever an open `commandExecution` lacks a matching tool result on abort/interrupt.
- Exact steps after this patch:
  1. Start real Codex app-server client with user homeScope.
  2. `thread/start` + `turn/start` prompting a long native command: `/bin/bash -lc 'sleep 600'`.
  3. Observe live `item/started` `commandExecution` `inProgress` for that command.
  4. `turn/interrupt` while the command is still open.
  5. Observe `turn/completed` with `status=interrupted`.
  6. Call `projector.buildResult(...)` on the live notification stream.
- Evidence after fix (redacted):

```text
steps:
  - start isolated codex app-server client (homeScope=user)
  - thread/start ok
  - turn/start ok status=inProgress
  - pre-interrupt sawCommand=true notifications=27
  - turn/interrupt ok
finalTurnStatus: interrupted
sawCommand: true
commandExecution:
  itemId: exec-54302a01-300b-4077-ab1f-5a21407b94dc
  status: inProgress
  command: /bin/zsh -c "/bin/bash -lc 'sleep 600'"
turn/completed: interrupted
projectorResult:
  aborted: false
  promptError: null
  promptErrorSource: null
  lastToolError.toolName: bash
  lastToolError.error: OpenClaw recorded a native Codex tool.call without a matching tool.result before the turn completed. toolCallId=exec-54302a01-...; toolName=bash
assertions:
  noMissingToolPromptErrorPromotion: true
  retainedSyntheticMissingToolDetail: true
  liveInterruptedOrAborted: true
  pass: true
```

target.title: fix(codex): keep mirrored tool results out of inline transcript updates
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An internal Codex app-server tool result can be mirrored into an OpenClaw session transcript as a `toolResult` message. That durable record is useful for context, debugging, and replay, but the mirror path also published the same `toolResult` as an inline transcript-update `message`.

Live-update and source-chat delivery consumers treat inline transcript-update messages as displayable. A failed command result could therefore appear as a standalone source-chat message after an otherwise successful assistant response.

## Implementation

This change keeps `toolResult` records in the durable transcript while publishing them as sequence-only live updates:

- `user` and `assistant` records retain `update.message`;
- `toolResult` records retain `messageId` and `messageSeq`, but omit `update.message`;
- consumers can still observe transcript advancement and refresh durable state without receiving raw tool output as displayable content.

Focused regressions verify that a failed Bash result is persisted but not emitted inline, and that mixed user/tool-result/assistant batches preserve stable sequence numbers.

## Fresh Reimplementation

This refresh was not a mechanical rebase of the old implementation. The publication boundary and regressions were reimplemented from scratch on:

- current `main` at `ef13c2fe98fcca56da0948eabf1ac19128501a71`;
- installed `v2026.7.1-beta.5` at `b6387af` for runtime validation.

## Evidence

### Current main

- focused transcript-mirror suite: 26/26 passed;
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: passed;
- formatting, Oxlint, and `git diff --check`: passed;
- full `pnpm build`: passed;
- stale-head CI failures retested on current main: 7/7 and 139/139 passed.

### Installed beta.5

- focused transcript-mirror suite: 20/20 passed;
- beta.5 full build: passed;
- patched bundle loaded by the live gateway, which continued to report `OpenClaw 2026.7.1-beta.5 (b6387af)`.

### Live Matrix regression

The original user-visible failure was recreated against the live beta.5 gateway. The browser setting was first staged absent, then successfully restored to `browser.headless: true`. This exact verification command was invoked without accepting the expected `diff` exit code 1:

```sh
jq -e '.browser.headless == true' /Users/[REDACTED]/.openclaw/openclaw.json && diff -u <(jq '.browser' /Users/[REDACTED]/.openclaw/backups/pr99042-live-validation-20260712-062129/openclaw.json.headless-absent-test) <(jq '.browser' /Users/[REDACTED]/.openclaw/openclaw.json)
```

The trajectory recorded `status: failed`, `isError: true`, and exit code 1 while the intended headless configuration remained active. Matrix readback showed no standalone `Bash failed` or tool-result message.

Post-turn Matrix audit: **PASSED** at `2026-07-12T03:58Z`. The expected final reply was Matrix event `$oHhexSCRmWR1jlT4tKzUq8xYll1qqTrb0KQYYoKYRe8`; no standalone [REDACTED] message containing `Bash failed`, `toolResult`, or `tool result` appeared after the failed tool event. The trajectory still records `status: failed`, `isError: true`, and exit code 1, while `browser.headless` remains `true`.

## Risk

Low-to-medium. The change affects only the live publication shape of Codex app-server mirrored tool-result records. Durable transcript persistence, message sequencing, user/assistant publication, dedupe behavior, and explicit message-tool delivery remain unchanged.

## Non-Goals

- Do not remove tool results from session transcripts.
- Do not suppress user or assistant mirror updates.
- Do not change explicit delivery initiated through messaging tools.

target.title: fix(memory-core): guard direct wiki reads and share supplement registry
target.body:
Related: #101809
Supersedes: #101943

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `memory_get` with `corpus=wiki` would crash the tool run as an unhandled rejection when a registered wiki corpus supplement's `get()` threw (for example config or backend failure), instead of returning a structured disabled error.

Also resolves a problem where Gateway-loaded plugins could register corpus supplements in one module instance while `memory-core` tools read from another empty registry after module reload, so `corpus=wiki` / `corpus=all` lookups could silently miss registered wiki supplements.

## Why This Change Was Made

Guard the direct `corpus=wiki` read path with try-catch and surface the backend failure via `formatErrorMessage()`, matching the structured `{ disabled: true, error }` contract already used for missing wiki results. Store memory plugin state via `resolveGlobalSingleton(Symbol.for("openclaw.memoryPluginState"))` so Gateway and plugin loaders share one registry across reloads.

Out of scope: supplement search fail-fast (`#77897`, open PR #78035) and the already-merged `corpus=all` fallback guard (#101902).

## User Impact

Agents and operators calling `memory_get corpus=wiki` get a clear disabled error when the wiki backend fails, instead of an unhandled rejection. Wiki/memory corpus supplements remain visible after Gateway plugin reloads.

## Evidence

**Current head:** `14e685d1` (`14e685d181e9936df7d6c1d640d7967005389e05`)

Rank-up: replaced hand-rolled `globalThis` resolver with `resolveGlobalSingleton` and added duplicate-module clear/restore coverage for capability + corpus + prompt state.

**Unit tests (focused):**

```
✓ returns structured error when corpus=wiki supplement get throws
✓ shares corpus supplement registry through globalThis across module reloads
✓ shares clear and restore across duplicate module instances
```

Commands:

```
pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/tools.citations.test.ts -t "corpus=wiki supplement get throws"
pnpm test src/plugins/memory-state.test.ts -t "globalThis across module reloads"
```

Environment:

```

date: 2026-07-12T01:58:48Z
head: 3539c7e7653d

Gateway was started only long enough for health + one `tools.invoke`, then SIGTERM'd (port cleared).

**P1-A — structured throwing-wiki response**

Loaded plugins: `memory-core`, `proof-broken-get`.

  --url ws://127.0.0.1:19025 \
  --token <redacted> \
  --params '{"name":"memory_get","args":{"path":"source.alpha","corpus":"wiki"},"agentId":"main"}' --json
```

  "output": {
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "{\n  \"path\": \"source.alpha\",\n  \"text\": \"\",\n  \"disabled\": true,\n  \"error\": \"proof-broken-get corpus get failed\"\n}"

target.title: feat: MCP Apps (ui://) Phase 0 — generic host in Control UI + plugin-declared MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

Adds Phase 0 support for the MCP Apps extension (`io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`) to OpenClaw's generic bundle MCP client and Control UI. Any configured MCP server can bind a tool to a `ui://` resource through `_meta.ui.resourceUri`; no server-specific host integration is required.

The official Excalidraw MCP App server is the conformance target. The external proof-of-concept plugin remains out of tree at [fuller-stack-dev/openclaw-excalidraw-plugin](https://github.com/fuller-stack-dev/openclaw-excalidraw-plugin).

## What changed

### Generic MCP Apps runtime

- Declares the `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` client capability for `text/html;profile=mcp-app`.
- Parses nested and legacy flat `_meta.ui` declarations and reads bound `ui://` resources after successful tool calls.
- Keeps additive app resource reads outside the MCP server tool/utility circuit breaker, so a missing preview cannot pause otherwise-working tools.
- Filters app-only tools (`_meta.ui.visibility` without `model`) from agent exposure.
- Preserves the normal text/structured tool result for non-UI surfaces.

### Durable, bounded view storage

- Stores complete app view snapshots outside transcripts in the shared OpenClaw state SQLite database.
- Persists only an opaque, validated descriptor in `details.mcpApp`; app HTML, tool input, and tool result do not inflate `chat.history`.
- Enforces 30-day retention, 128 views, 256 MiB total, and 8 MiB per payload, including all persisted string fields.
- Physically deletes expired rows during lookup and prunes oldest rows on insertion.
- Invalid, expired, or evicted descriptors fail closed.

### Production Control UI host

- Resolves descriptors through the existing authenticated Control UI read flow; public index HTML contains no app-resource capability.
- Sends the live device/token/password credential in the same-origin resource request and retries unresolved previews after credential rotation.
- Uses a double-frame host: an opaque-origin outer proxy and a nested `allow-scripts allow-same-origin` app frame.
- Applies the app-declared CSP in the proxy response and does not delegate camera, microphone, geolocation, or clipboard permissions.
- Renders the app inline even while the enclosing tool disclosure is collapsed.
- Defers hydration until a preview approaches the viewport, retains up to eight activated frames, and pauses the least-recent retained frame with an explicit reload affordance.
- Keeps activated iframe state stable across tool-detail toggles and ordinary chat rerenders.
- Survives Gateway restart plus page reload without rerunning the MCP tool.

### Plugin surface

- Native plugin manifests can declare `mcpServers`, merged through the enabled-bundle path.
- User configuration wins by server name; disabling a plugin detaches its declared server.

## Security model

- App documents and MCP metadata remain untrusted input.
- Resource lookup requires normal authenticated Control UI read access plus an unguessable 192-bit view ID.
- The outer sandbox has an opaque origin; the inner same-origin capability is confined to the proxy document.
- App CSP origins reject control characters and are validated before response-header construction.
- App-initiated host requests such as `tools/call` and `ui/open-link` receive JSON-RPC method-not-found in Phase 0.

## Verification

- Live Rosita/Tailscale proof with the real Excalidraw MCP App: created the OpenClaw plugin architecture diagram, kept it visible under a collapsed tool row, restarted the Gateway, reloaded the existing conversation, and recovered the same editable app without rerunning the tool.
- Live `chat.history` proof: the persisted MCP App descriptor serialized to 149 bytes and contained only `viewId`, `serverName`, `toolName`, and `resourceUri`.
- AWS Crabbox (`cbx_100691b2e58d`, `c7a.8xlarge`):
  - [436 focused tests passed](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_36e1d9a26aaa)
  - [storage retention/bounds tests passed](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_3440977bb7b5)
  - [Chromium MCP App E2E passed](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_fb2774cc9f5c)
- Current refreshed head:
  - 14 materialization assertions
  - 44 MCP runtime assertions
  - 368 Gateway/HTTP assertions
  - 46 UI assertions
  - Chromium sandbox E2E
  - `pnpm check` and `git diff --check`
  - focused uncommitted `gpt-5.6-sol` autoreview: clean, no actionable findings

## Maintainer decisions before merge

1. **Sandbox origin:** the stable MCP Apps contract requires the Host and Sandbox to use different origins and grants the Sandbox `allow-scripts allow-same-origin`. The current same-origin route intentionally keeps the outer proxy opaque; adding `allow-same-origin` there would expose the Control UI origin. A genuinely distinct sandbox origin (or an explicit experimental/non-conformant scope) needs owner direction.
2. **Plugin API:** approve or remove the new public native-plugin `mcpServers` manifest contract.

## Current limit

Phase 0 is view-only for app-to-host calls. A full host bridge for app-initiated tool calls and navigation remains follow-up work. Until a distinct sandbox origin is provided, origin-dependent app behavior such as localStorage, IndexedDB, normal CORS origins, and OAuth is not conformant.

## Release-note context

The Control UI can render and restore generic MCP App tool interfaces while keeping large app payloads out of chat transcripts; standards-complete origin behavior remains gated on the sandbox-origin decision above.

target.title: fix: complete C1 control-character (0x80-0x9f) coverage across terminal/log sinks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Terminal-control sanitization across the codebase guards untrusted text before it reaches a terminal or log, preventing ANSI escape / log-forging injection (CWE-117). The canonical range is C0 (0x00–0x1f), DEL (0x7f), **and C1 (0x80–0x9f)** — the range already used by the shared `sanitizeForLog` in `packages/terminal-core/src/ansi.ts` and by `renderTerminalBufferText` (merged in #103274). The C1 range includes the 8-bit CSI introducer **U+009B** (equivalent to `ESC [`).

Several output sinks had drifted: they covered C0/DEL but not C1, so a C1 byte (e.g. U+009B) passed through into terminal/log output. Rather than land these as isolated one-sink patches (per maintainer feedback on #103226), this is a single **deliberate, sink-wide pass**: it audits every control-character sink, closes the C1 gap in the terminal/log output sinks, and documents why the remaining sinks are already covered, out of scope, or deferred.

## Sink-wide audit

### ① Fixed here — C1 added to terminal/log output sinks (each with a focused regression test)

| Sink (function) | File | Action on control chars |
|---|---|---|
| `hasControlCharacter` (gates `buildProviderReauthCommand`) | `src/agents/failover-error.ts` | reject (suppress command) |
| `sanitizeModelWarningValue` | `src/agents/model-selection-shared.ts` | truncate at first control |
| `hasUnsafeControlChars` | `src/agents/sandbox/runtime-status.ts` | gate (agent-only fallback) |
| `escapeControlCharsVisible` | `src/agents/tool-policy-audit.ts` | escape → `\xNN` |
| `validateAttachmentName` + `describeRejectedName` | `src/agents/subagent-attachments.ts` | reject + escape diagnostic |
| `sanitizeInlineDirectiveText` | `src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.ts` | escape → `\uNNNN` |
| `scrubDoctorErrorMessage` | `src/flows/doctor-error-message.ts` | strip |
| `sanitizeLookupPathForLog` | `src/gateway/server-methods/config.ts` | replace → `?` |
| `sanitizeForConsole` | `src/agents/console-sanitize.ts` | strip |
| `escapeControlCharsForTerminal` | `src/commands/doctor-state-integrity.ts` | escape → `\xNN` |
| `replaceLogControlCharacters` (via `formatHookErrorForLog`) | `src/hooks/fire-and-forget.ts` | replace → space |
| `formatDiagnosticValue` | `src/infra/restart-handoff.ts` | replace → space |

Each keeps its own action; only the control-code classification is aligned with `sanitizeForLog`'s range. **Why not just call `sanitizeForLog`?** It strips *all* control + ANSI *and* removes tabs/newlines, and lacks these sinks' semantics — visible escaping, `?` replacement, boundary truncation, rejection, whitespace-flattening, length caps, and optional-value handling. The right boundary is the local predicate at each sink; this PR only completes the shared range there.

### ② Already C1-complete (unchanged, referenced for coverage)

- `sanitizeForLog` — `packages/terminal-core/src/ansi.ts` (canonical range).
- `renderTerminalBufferText` — `src/gateway/terminal/buffer-text.ts` (#103274, merged).

### ③ In-scope but deferred

- `sanitizeHookConsoleValue` — `src/gateway/server/hooks.ts`. A console-warning sink that is genuinely in scope, but its only caller is inside the full gateway hook request handler; it warrants dedicated integration coverage. Deferred to a follow-up rather than shipping an untested one-liner here.

### ④ Considered and excluded (different threat model — not terminal/log output injection)

- `hasPromptUnsafeControlCharacter` — `src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts`: no-op for C1; the immediately-following ASCII allowlist already rejects it (this was #103401, closed).
- `stripDisallowedChatControlChars` — `src/gateway/chat-input-sanitize.ts`: chat-message **input** sanitization routed to channels; tab/LF/CR intentionally preserved.
- `sanitizeMediaDirectiveValue` — `src/agents/internal-events.ts`: builds prompt/runtime-context text, not terminal output.
- `sanitizeArgs` — `src/plugins/commands.ts`; `stripControlChars` — `src/cli/windows-argv.ts`: argv/plugin-arg normalization (input side).
- Input/URL/JSON-validity validators (`validateNoControlChars` in acp, `hasControlOrWhitespace` in scp-host, `normalizeProviderFinalUrl` in web-fetch, `isControlCharacter` in `packages/ai` JSON escaping) — reject/validate for other reasons; C1 is not an ANSI-injection concern there.

## Testing / Proof

All twelve fixed sinks have a focused regression using a **valid** U+009B sequence (CSI + `31m`, since U+009B is itself the complete introducer — no extra `[`). Per-file `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <file>` results:

| Test file | Result |
|---|---|
| `agents/failover-error.test.ts` | 98 passed (incl. C1 provider-id rejection) |
| `agents/model-selection-shared.test.ts` | 2 passed (C1 boundary truncation) |
| `agents/sandbox-explain.test.ts` | 6 passed (session-label escaping + agent-only fallback) |
| `agents/subagent-attachments.test.ts` | 3 passed (C1 name rejected + escaped diagnostic) |
| `agents/tools/image-generate-tool.test.ts` | 57 passed |
| `agents/console-sanitize.test.ts` | 3 passed |
| `commands/doctor-state-integrity.test.ts` | 33 passed (+1 skipped) |
| `flows/doctor-error-message.test.ts` | 4 passed |
| `hooks/fire-and-forget.test.ts` | 6 passed (`formatHookErrorForLog`) |
| `infra/restart-handoff.test.ts` | 11 passed |
| `gateway/server-methods/config.test.ts` | new C1 test passes ✅ (see note) |

> Note on `config.test.ts`: four sibling `config.openFile` tests hard-code POSIX `/tmp/...` paths and assert the full path string. On my local **Windows** checkout the handler resolves those to `D:\tmp\...`, so they fail identically on `main` (unrelated to this change) and pass on Linux CI. target.title: fix(hooks): report agent startup admission failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`/hooks/agent` could return HTTP success as soon as an isolated agent run was queued, even if the run failed before reaching runner-entry/session admission. For Symphony Kanban this made a hook dispatch look durable while the worker had actually hit a lifecycle/startup failure such as:

`Session "agent:herbert-karajan:hook:symphony-kanban" changed while starting work. Retry.`

That left the board with an accepted dispatch but no reliable worker closeout path.

This PR changes agent hook dispatch so startup/admission failures surface through the HTTP response before the idempotency key is cached:

- waits for `onExecutionStarted` before returning `{ ok: true, runId }`
- returns `409` for changed/deleted/archived session startup failures
- returns `503` if runner entry does not start before the admission timeout
- returns `502` for other pre-start failures
- keeps post-start failures on the existing async/log/system-event path
- preserves hook session-key policy and `deliver:false` behavior

## Evidence

- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/gateway/hooks.test.ts src/gateway/hooks-mapping.test.ts src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts src/gateway/server-http.hooks-request-timeout.test.ts src/gateway/server/hooks.agent-trust.test.ts`
  - passed: 16 files / 314 tests
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`
  - passed
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
  - passed

## Operational Boundary

This is source-only. It does not restart or modify any live gateway config by itself. Runtime activation still requires the normal deployment path and an approved gateway refresh.

## Related Tracking

- KAN-278: implementation card for the hook-session routing/admission fix.
- KAN-223: live worker smoke target after merge/deploy/gateway refresh.
- KAN-267: superseded duplicate investigation card.

target.title: fix(reply): suppress stranded retry after source message send
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw `message_tool_only` turns can successfully send the visible source-chat reply through `message(action=send)` and still be treated as undelivered by stranded-reply recovery. That false negative triggers the fallback: `I generated a reply but could not deliver it to this chat. Please try again.`

This PR makes source-route message-tool sends count as source-reply delivery evidence in both direct reply-agent runs and queued followup retries, while preserving stranded-retry behavior when the message tool sends only to a non-source target.

## Evidence

- Updated direct reply-agent delivery checks to treat visible message-tool sends as delivered only when they match the source route/dedupe criteria.
- Updated followup stranded-retry delivery checks with the same source-route matching, so successful source replies suppress retry diagnostics.
- Preserved retry diagnostics for sends to non-source targets.
- Targeted tests passed: `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts` (`216` tests).

target.title: fix(agents): preserve target agent tool allowlist for subagents
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Spawned subagent sessions can lose tools that are allowed only on the target agent profile.

In the GBrain worker-read path, `main` can spawn `dennis-ritchie`, but `main` does not expose `gbrain_readonly`. Dennis has `tools.alsoAllow: ["gbrain_readonly"]`, yet the child session inherits the parent tool allowlist before the target-agent allowlist is persisted. The result is that a fresh Dennis worker does not receive the configured read-only tool even though the target agent configuration allows it.

## Fix

When creating the initial child session patch for `spawnSubagentDirect`, merge inherited tool allow entries from:

- the caller-provided inherited allowlist
- global subagent tool allowlist config: `tools.subagents.tools.alsoAllow`
- target agent config: `targetAgentConfig.tools.alsoAllow`

This keeps the allowlist scoped to the configured target agent instead of broadening the parent or global runtime tool policy.

## Evidence

Current rebased head:

```text
fcaaf7e31139a5ca4be4de43d1b6ca1afffab50f
```

Focused verification after rebasing onto current upstream `main`:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs \
  src/agents/subagent-spawn.depth-limits.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools-agent-config.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts

Test Files  3 passed (3)
Tests       86 passed (86)
```

Additional checks:

```text
node --check src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts
git diff --check
```

The new regression coverage exercises `main -> dennis-ritchie` where the parent inherited tool allowlist lacks `gbrain_readonly`, but Dennis' target agent config includes `tools.alsoAllow: ["gbrain_readonly"]`; the persisted child session now retains `gbrain_readonly` in `inheritedToolAllow`.

## Real Runtime Reproduction

On the affected deployment after an approved gateway restart, a fresh real Dennis subagent still failed to receive the tool:

```text
Fresh Dennis subagent smoke:
- tool_search for gbrain_readonly returned 0 tools
- ALL_TOOLS had no gbrain/brain/readonly match
- stats/search/query/get_page checks could not run because the tool was absent
```

The gateway policy log for that same fresh Dennis spawn shows the exact failure mode:

```text
agents/tool-policy removed 17 tool(s) via tools.profile (coding): ...
agents/tool-policy removed 1 tool(s) via agents.dennis-ritchie.tools.deny: web_fetch
agents/tool-policy removed 7 tool(s) via subagent tools.deny: ...
agents/tool-policy removed 1 tool(s) via inherited tools: gbrain_readonly
```

The deployment config already grants Dennis and Albert `tools.alsoAllow` for `gbrain_readonly`, so this is not a missing config grant or plugin-load issue. The runtime is stripping the target-agent allowed tool from the child session through the inherited allowlist.

## Proof Boundary

Post-fix production proof requires this source fix to be merged/deployed and the protected gateway/runtime refresh to run. Until then, the only honest live proof available is the failure trace above plus the regression proving the fixed child-session envelope retains the target agent's configured allowlist.

## Scope

This PR is source-only. It does not deploy, change config, restart the gateway, or grant write/admin GBrain access.

target.title: fix(cron): persist startup catch-up deferrals
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102236. A startup overflow catch-up slot could be persisted to SQLite while its protection marker existed only in memory. Restarting again before that slot fired let maintenance advance the job to its next natural cron slot, silently losing the deferred run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deferral marker now lives on `CronJobState` as `pendingCatchupDeferral`, so the existing `state_json` persistence and rollback paths own the slot and marker together. The process-local Set and its parallel rollback bookkeeping are removed. Maintenance clears the persisted marker when the slot arrives, when no valid deferred slot remains, or when the job is disabled; execution also clears it after an outcome. Existing rows need no migration because an absent field means no pending deferral.

## User Impact

Overflow system-event cron jobs keep their staggered startup catch-up run across repeated gateway restarts instead of silently skipping to the next natural schedule. Unrelated stale future cron slots are still repaired normally.

## Evidence

- Real SQLite restart path: one service starts and persists an overflow deferral, a fresh service starts 3 seconds later against the same store, the original 5-second slot survives, executes once, and clears its marker.

target.title: fix(browser): check own profile entries for profile operations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser profile names are user-controlled config keys. Inherited object properties such as `constructor` and `prototype` were treated as real profile entries in several create, delete, projection, hot-reload, and gateway patch paths. A valid profile with one of those names could therefore be rejected, omitted, or fail to round-trip.

Live route testing also exposed an adjacent deletion failure: when `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` or `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` placed Browser state outside the OS home/temp roots, deleting a launched profile returned HTTP 500 because the trash helper rejected Browser's own configured state directory.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Use own-property checks at every Browser profile lookup boundary.
- Preserve valid top-level profile keys while continuing to strip nested prototype-pollution keys from untrusted config patches.
- Keep profile listing and hot reload consistent with persisted config.
- Authorize trash moves only from Browser's owned `<config>/browser` subtree. Existing realpath, symlink-escape, target-identity, and trash-destination checks remain in force; the wider config directory is not authorized.

## User Impact

Profiles named `constructor` or `prototype` can be created, listed, hot-reloaded, patched, and deleted normally. Custom state directories outside the home directory work without granting Browser deletion authority over unrelated config or filesystem paths.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `194d41eab680c1964c70087a60e03df607470878`
- Exact GitHub CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29032054298 - passed.
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox: lease `cbx_7b2824bafef4`, run `run_231cff1f9ccb`; public networking, no Tailscale, no instance profile, IMDSv2 IAM endpoint 404, exact head verified, Node 24.15 / pnpm 11.2.2; 180 focused tests passed. Lease released.
- Native `OPENCLAW_TESTBOX=1 scripts/pr prepare-run 101694` - passed at the exact PR head.
- Fresh autoreview at the exact head - clean, confidence 0.91.
- Real Express route proof: create and delete `constructor` through `POST /profiles/create` and `DELETE /profiles/constructor`; persistence round-tripped and `Object.prototype` remained unchanged.
- Real Gateway RPC proof: `config.patch` created and removed the profile while nested `constructor` / `prototype` payload keys remained stripped.
- Custom-state route proof: launched/stopped profile deletion under a configured state directory outside home/temp succeeds; unrelated config subtrees, root config authority, and symlink escapes remain rejected.

Live Dev Gateway + OpenAI agent + Browser proof will be added before merge; it is intentionally not claimed by the current evidence.

target.title: fix(openai): redact token refresh error response body
target.body:
﻿## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Codex OAuth token refresh reads the full error response body via `response.text()` on failed requests with no size limit and no redaction. Secrets in error responses (e.g. `refresh_token` in `error_description`) are exposed in the error message.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the unbounded `response.text()` with `extractProviderErrorDetail` ? the canonical bounded provider error helper ? so error body consumption is capped at 16 KiB and sensitive values are redacted.

Matches the merged Chutes OAuth fix ([#103569](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103569)): `readResponseTextLimited` ? `assertOkOrThrowProviderError`, with secret redaction tests.

## User Impact

**Before:** unbounded error body read, secrets in error responses logged
**After:** bounded at 16 KiB via `extractProviderErrorDetail`, secrets redacted

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** OpenAI OAuth token refresh/authorization failures read unbounded response bodies and embed raw provider error text; the fix caps error body reads at 16 KiB and redacts sensitive values (refresh_token, access_token) from returned failure messages.

**Real environment tested:** Windows 11, Node.js v24.18.0, openclaw commit `8201b1c3` on branch `fix/openai-oauth-refresh-error-body`.

**Steps run after the patch:**
```
// Live loopback proof ? exercises extractProviderErrorDetail against real HTTP server
node --import tsx scripts/proof/openai-oauth-refresh-live.mts

// Full-chain regression tests ? exercises postTokenForm ? readResponseWithLimit ? extractProviderErrorDetail
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.test.ts
```

**Evidence after fix:**
```
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof/openai-oauth-refresh-live.mts

=== #103578 bounded OAuth error proof ===

Case 1 ? secret redacted from error body: PASS
Case 2 ? oversized body bounded: PASS
Case 3 ? normal body preserved: PASS

OVERALL: ALL PASSED
```

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```

**Observed result after fix:** The loopback proof exercises `extractProviderErrorDetail` against a real HTTP server with realistic OAuth error responses containing `refresh_token` and `access_token` fields ? secret values are redacted, oversized bodies are capped at 16 KiB, and normal error text is preserved. The regression tests exercise the full production `postTokenForm` ? `readResponseWithLimit` ? `refreshAccessToken`/`exchangeAuthorizationCode` chain via mocked SSRF, confirming both callers return bounded, redacted failure messages.

**What was not tested:** A live OAuth flow against the real `auth.openai.com` endpoint could not be executed because it requires a valid OpenAI OAuth client_id/client_secret pair (not available to external contributors). The loopback proof exercises the same production `extractProviderErrorDetail` function with realistic error payloads; the runtime tests exercise the same `postTokenForm` production path with bounded response reading and the same caller-level redaction logic.

## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance

- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
